Name: Numidian Saddleless Light Cavalry: Javelin Mobility and Guerrilla Tactics of Luring the Enemy
RagShortTexts: Numidian riders wore no heavy armor and used no saddle, controlling their horses with only a leather cord or grass bridle
Riding at speed to circle around, they wore down heavy legions with continuous javelin volleys and feigned retreats
On the battlefields of Cannae and Zama they repeatedly carried out deep encirclements and rolled up the enemy, deciding the outcome
BaseText: Numidian light cavalry were the light horsemen with the greatest mobile deterrent power in the classical age. They were small, lean and tough, wore coarse woolen cloaks, and carried round leather shields and several poisoned short javelins. Astonishingly, the Numidians used neither heavy saddles nor stirrups; with only a thin leather cord or a woven grass rein around the horse's neck, and slight pressure of their legs to shift their weight, they became one with their swift little North African horses and moved over rocky desert as if on level ground. In battle they never clashed head-on with Roman heavy infantry, but wheeled and galloped like locusts, throwing javelins with precision at the enemy's flanks and rear while at full gallop; as soon as the enemy organized a counterattack, they at once scattered in a feigned rout, luring the enemy formation into breaking apart, and then, when the enemy was exhausted, suddenly turned back and surrounded them. Hannibal used these mobile tactics to the fullest at the Trebia and at Cannae.

Variants.Content: The wind is our guide and the horse is our legs! The heavy Roman infantry will never touch a hair on our heads, and our javelins always drink blood in the gaps between their shields!

These barefoot African demons on horseback are as cunning as foxes and wolves! They never stay in one place; when you chase them they flee, and when you stop, their flying javelins come whistling at your back.
General Hannibal's most loyal hounds! As long as the Numidian cavalry seal off both wings, the Romans' backs are completely exposed to our killing blades.
